founder_story.core_moment: Jesse and his wife would miss Reuben after putting him in his crib, then spend up to an hour in bed moving backward through Apple Photos from that day to his birth.
founder_story.product_origin: The camera roll could replay the media but could not preserve the parents' memories and meaning around it. Jesse imagined a baby company that could use new technology to create exceptional experiences for parents, beginning with Our Little World.

The hour after bedtime that became Our Little World
Why I started Our Little World
emails.preview: After we put Reuben in his crib, my wife and I would get into bed, open Apple Photos, and scroll all the way back to his birth.
preview_alternatives: After we put Reuben in his crib, my wife and I would get into bed, open Apple Photos, and scroll all the way back to his birth.
The camera roll brought the moments back. It could not hold everything we wanted to remember.
emails.headline: We built this because **the photo was never the whole memory.**
paragraphs: After my wife and I put our son, Reuben, in his crib, we would get into bed—and **almost immediately start missing him.**
We would open Apple Photos, watch the videos from that day, and keep scrolling backward: yesterday, last month, all the way to his birth. **Sometimes an hour disappeared like that.**

The photos brought the moments back. But they could not hold the things we were saying to each other while we looked: **the details only we knew, what made us laugh, how a season felt**, and what we hoped we would never forget.

I kept thinking there had to be a better way to keep the story around the photos. Then the idea grew: what if we built a baby company that could use the latest technology carefully to create genuinely wonderful experiences for parents—beginning with **a private place for these memories?** That is where Our Little World was born.
You do not need to rebuild the past tonight. Choose one photo that still makes you feel something and add the sentence you would tell someone who was not there. **That is enough to begin.**

emails.headline: The camera kept the scene. **You kept the meaning.**
paragraphs: When my wife and I looked through photos of Reuben, we would stop on the same image and start telling each other **what had happened around it.**
One of us remembered the routine. The other remembered a look, a sound, or why we had taken the photo in the first place. **The image held the scene; our conversation held the memory.**

Try that with one ordinary photo from the last few days. Add the detail only you would know: what was happening just outside the frame, what had become part of the daily rhythm, or why this small moment stayed with you.
That sentence is **not a caption for an audience.** It is a note to your future family.

emails.headline: Your family story should remain **yours to choose.**
paragraphs: If I was going to build a product around our son's photos and memories, the first rule had to be simple: **Reuben's story is not something for a public feed.**

Technology should do quiet work for a family—not take the story away from them. In Our Little World, **you choose the photo access** on your device. You can add a photo manually, or use optional discovery to surface likely moments for review.

Selected manual imports and calibrated auto-saves can enter the private family archive. Nothing is posted to a public feed. If broader library access does not feel right, **keep it limited and choose photos yourself.**
The product should earn trust through clear choices. **You should never have to trade control for convenience.**

emails.headline: One day. **Two memories.**
paragraphs: Looking through Reuben's photos with my wife taught me something obvious that I had never really noticed: **we lived the same day, but we did not remember the same things.**
She would hold a detail I had missed. I would remember why a moment mattered to me. **Neither version was the complete story on its own.**
That is why Our Little World is built for a small private family space, not one default memory keeper. Invite the person who holds the other perspective.
The goal is not a larger audience. It is **a fuller story of the same little world.**

emails.headline: A milestone is the label. **The detail is the story.**
paragraphs: The photo I shared earlier says eleven months on a little wooden sign. It marks the age beautifully. **But the number is not the whole memory.**
A milestone photo cannot automatically keep what changed that month, what the family had started noticing, or the story everyone will tell later.
That is the idea behind Firsts. Record one change, then add the detail that makes it belong to your family: **where you were, what happened around it, or the words you kept using afterward.**
The milestone is the label. **The detail is what brings your little world back.**

emails.headline: A letter can begin with **one true sentence.**
paragraphs: When I think about Letters, I imagine Reuben reading something we wrote while he was small and hearing the people we were then—**not polished authors, just his parents trying to notice him well.**
That sounds important, which can make it hard to begin. So do not start with a letter.
Our Little World should never turn loving your family into homework. It should **help you keep what matters, then get out of the way.**
If it is helping—or still asking too much—reply and tell me. I am building this as Reuben's dad, and I want it to feel worthy of the families who trust it.

Verify support@ourlittleworld.me is monitored before sending reply invitations.
Implement explicit marketing-consent capture and server-authored audience eligibility; product account creation alone is insufficient.
Synchronize moment_saved exits and coarse role/permission state without sending private family content to Mailchimp.
Add privacy-safe caregiver invite, first_created, and letter_created outcome events before enabling those skips.
Keep gift purchase, gift delivery, redemption, billing, export, deletion, and security communications transactional and separate.
Render, link-check, accessibility-check, and inspect every HTML and plain-text version.
Send controlled tests to verified internal recipients and inspect receipt in representative clients.
